sections.text_helper: Section 39.3.2 "RTC pins and internal signals" in chapter 39 (Real-time clock (RTC)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1553.
sections.section_content:
[Table 390. RTC input/output pins]
RTC_OUT1 and RTC_OUT2 which select one of the following two outputs:
• CALIB: 512Hz or 1Hz clock output (with an LSE frequency of 32.768kHz). This output
is enabled by setting the COE bit in the RTC_CR register.
• TAMPALRM: This output is the OR between rtc_tamp_evt and ALARM signals.
ALARM is enabled by configuring the OSEL[1:0] bits in the RTC_CR register which select
the alarm A, alarm B or wake-up outputs. rtc_tamp_evt is enabled by setting the TAMPOE
bit in the RTC_CR register which selects the tamper event outputs.
[Table 391. RTC internal input/output signals]
The RTC kernel clock is usually the LSE at 32.768kHz although it is possible to select other
clock sources in the RCC (refer to RCC for more details). Some functions are not available
in some low-power modes when the selected clock is not LSE. Refer to Section39.4: RTC
low-power modes for more details.
[Table 392. RTC interconnection]
The triggers outputs can be used as triggers for other peripherals.
